query: Which linear solves or Cholesky factorizations will use selective double or mixed precision, what numeric thresholds prompt higher precision, and how will you measure tradeoffs vs throughput?

response.query: Which linear solves or Cholesky factorizations will use selective double or mixed precision, what numeric thresholds prompt higher precision, and how will you measure tradeoffs vs throughput?
response.answer: Linear solves and Cholesky factorizations may use mixed precision when numerical thresholds indicate instability, typically when condition numbers exceed certain limits. Tradeoffs vs throughput are measured by balancing precision and computational speed. Mixed precision helps optimize performance.
